name: WiFi Reconnaissance
description: Ability to perform wireless network discovery and reconnaissance. Covers passive and active scanning of 802.11 networks, SSID enumeration, client identification, channel mapping, signal strength analysis, and identification of security configurations advertised in beacons and probe responses (WPA2, WPA3, WPS, management frame protection). PMKID capture and handshake attacks belong to WSEC-WIFI-WPA. Provides the situational awareness needed for all subsequent WiFi security assessments.

0.label: None
0.description: No exposure to WiFi reconnaissance techniques

1.label: Awareness
1.description: Understands 802.11 network architecture and the purpose of wireless reconnaissance
evidence: Can describe 802.11 frame types (management, control, data) and their roles
Understands the difference between passive and active scanning
Completed training on WiFi fundamentals and security assessment methodology

2.label: Guided Practice
2.description: Performs WiFi reconnaissance using standard tools under supervision
evidence: Configured monitor mode on wireless adapters and captured 802.11 frames under guidance
Used airodump-ng or equivalent to enumerate networks, clients, and security settings
Identified WPA2, WPA3, WPS, and open networks from captured beacons under supervision

3.label: Independent Practice
3.description: Independently conducts comprehensive WiFi reconnaissance across target environments
evidence: Independently performed WiFi reconnaissance for 3+ engagements producing complete network maps
Identified hidden SSIDs, client associations, and roaming patterns
Mapped channel utilization and signal coverage across physical spaces
Produced reconnaissance reports documenting all discovered networks and their security posture

4.label: Advanced / Mentor
4.description: Conducts advanced reconnaissance across complex multi-site environments; develops recon automation
evidence: Performed reconnaissance in high-density enterprise environments with hundreds of access points
Developed automated scanning and reporting scripts for WiFi reconnaissance
Identified non-standard or rogue 802.11 implementations through frame analysis
Reviews reconnaissance findings of junior staff and mentors on technique selection

5.label: Expert / Authority
5.description: Defines WiFi reconnaissance methodology; develops novel discovery techniques
evidence: Authored the lab's WiFi reconnaissance methodology and tooling standards
Developed novel passive fingerprinting or network discovery techniques
Published research on 802.11 reconnaissance or wireless network mapping
Trains teams on WiFi reconnaissance and operational security considerations

assessment_methods.description: Perform comprehensive WiFi reconnaissance in a controlled lab environment and produce a complete network inventory with security assessments
Observe WiFi reconnaissance setup, tool configuration, and passive/active scanning technique execution

equipment: Alfa AWUS036ACH or equivalent monitor-mode-capable WiFi adapter
Directional WiFi antenna for signal source location
